questions.title: JSON Parse Number Field
questions.description:
Read a single-line JSON object with an `x` field. Parse it with the JSON module and print the value of `x`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a JSON object like {"x": 5}.

Output Format:
The integer value of the `x` field.

Constraints:
x is an integer between 0 and 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
require "json"
obj = JSON.parse(gets.chomp)
puts obj["x"]

questions.title: Date Weekday Number
questions.description:
Read three integers y, m, d. Construct a Date object for that calendar day and print its weekday number using `wday` (0 = Sunday, 6 = Saturday).

Input Format:
Line 1: y m d (year month day).

Output Format:
A single integer 0..6 (the weekday).

Constraints:
Valid Gregorian date between 1900-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.sourcecode:
require "date"
y, m, d = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
date = Date.new(y, m, d)
puts date.wday

questions.title: CSV Row Count Temp File
questions.description:
Read n, then n lines of comma-separated values. Write them to /tmp/atom_ruby_csv1.csv, read the file back with CSV.read, and print the number of rows.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: CSV rows.

Output Format:
The number of CSV rows read back.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; each row has at least 1 column.

questions.title: Time Hour Minute Format
questions.description:
Read two integers h and m. Construct a Time for January 1, 2024 at h:m:00 using Time.new, then print it formatted as HH:MM (24-hour, zero-padded) using strftime.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers h and m.

Output Format:
A 5-character string HH:MM.

Constraints:
0 <= h <= 23; 0 <= m <= 59.
questions.sourcecode:
require "time"
h, m = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
t = Time.new(2024, 1, 1, h, m, 0)
puts t.strftime("%H:%M")

questions.title: YAML Load Hash Value
questions.description:
Read a YAML document from stdin containing a hash with key `x`. Parse it with the YAML module and print the value of `x`.

Input Format:
One or more lines of YAML describing a hash with an integer `x` field.

Output Format:
The integer value of `x`.

Constraints:
x is an integer between 0 and 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
require "yaml"
data = $stdin.read
obj = YAML.load(data)
puts obj["x"]

questions.title: Benchmark Sum of Squares
questions.description:
Read an integer n. Use Benchmark.measure to time the computation of the sum of squares 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2 (the timing itself is ignored). Print the integer result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.

Output Format:
The integer sum of squares from 1 to n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
require "benchmark"
n = gets.to_i
result = 0
Benchmark.measure do
  (1..n).each { |x| result += x * x }
end
puts result

questions.title: JSON Service Config Printer
questions.description:
A microservice's config is a JSON object with `name` and `port` fields. Parse the JSON and print a banner line: "<name> on port <port>".

Input Format:
Line 1: a JSON object like {"name":"api","port":8080}.

Output Format:
A single line: name followed by " on port " and the port number.

Constraints:
name is a non-empty string; 1 <= port <= 65535.
questions.sourcecode:
require "json"
obj = JSON.parse(gets.chomp)
puts "#{obj['name']} on port #{obj['port']}"

questions.title: Date Difference In Days
questions.description:
Two calendar dates are provided. Construct Date objects for both and print the integer number of days from the first date to the second date (positive if the second is later).

Input Format:
Line 1: y1 m1 d1 y2 m2 d2.

Output Format:
The integer difference date2 - date1 in days.

Constraints:
Valid dates between 1900-01-01 and 2100-12-31.
questions.sourcecode:
require "date"
y1, m1, d1, y2, m2, d2 = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
date1 = Date.new(y1, m1, d1)
date2 = Date.new(y2, m2, d2)
puts (date2 - date1).to_i

questions.title: CSV Column Sum Temp File
questions.description:
A shop keeps n line items as CSV rows with two columns: name and amount. Write the rows to /tmp/atom_ruby_csv2.csv, read them back with CSV.read, sum the second column, and print the total.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: name,amount CSV rows.

Output Format:
The integer sum of all amounts.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 0 <= amount <= 1000.

questions.title: YAML Config Version Banner
questions.description:
A release config file is a YAML document with `name` and `version` keys. Parse the document with the YAML module and print "<name> v<version>".

Input Format:
A YAML document on one or more lines with `name` (string) and `version` (integer) keys.

Output Format:
A single banner line: name, space, 'v', version.

Constraints:
name is a lowercase string 1..20 chars; 1 <= version <= 99.
questions.sourcecode:
require "yaml"
data = $stdin.read
obj = YAML.load(data)
puts "#{obj['name']} v#{obj['version']}"

questions.title: JSON Nested Inventory Sum
questions.description:
A warehouse inventory comes as a JSON object with an `items` array; each item has a `qty` integer. Parse the JSON and print the total of all item quantities.

Input Format:
Line 1: a JSON object like {"items":[{"qty":3},{"qty":5}]}.

Output Format:
The integer sum of all qty fields.

Constraints:
1 <= items.length <= 100; 1 <= qty <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
require "json"
obj = JSON.parse(gets.chomp)
total = 0
obj["items"].each { |item| total += item["qty"] }
puts total

questions.title: Date Business Days Counter
questions.description:
Count weekday days (Monday through Friday) in the inclusive range [start, finish] constructed from two dates. Iterate the date range and count days whose wday is 1..5.

Input Format:
Line 1: y1 m1 d1 y2 m2 d2 (start then finish).

Output Format:
The number of Mon-Fri days in the inclusive range.

Constraints:
Valid dates 1900-01-01 to 2100-12-31; range span <= 365 days.
questions.sourcecode:
require "date"
y1, m1, d1, y2, m2, d2 = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
start = Date.new(y1, m1, d1)
finish = Date.new(y2, m2, d2)
count = 0
(start..finish).each do |d|
  count += 1 if d.wday >= 1 && d.wday <= 5
end
puts count

questions.title: CSV Group By Category Sum
questions.description:
Sales records come as n CSV rows with two columns: category and amount. Write the rows to /tmp/atom_ruby_csv3.csv, read them back with CSV.read, group amounts by category (sum per category), and print "<category> <total>" lines sorted by category.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: category,amount CSV rows.

Output Format:
One line per unique category, sorted, as "category total".

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; lowercase category names; 1 <= amount <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
lines = []
n.times { lines << gets.chomp }
path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_csv3.csv"
File.open(path, "w") do |f|
  lines.each { |l| f.puts(l) }
end
rows = File.readlines(path).map { |l| l.chomp.split(",") }
groups = {}
rows.each do |row|
  cat = row[0]
  amt = row[1].to_i
  groups[cat] = 0 unless groups.key?(cat)
  groups[cat] += amt
end
keys = groups.keys.sort
keys.each { |k| puts "#{k} #{groups[k]}" }

questions.title: YAML Nested Database Config
questions.description:
A database config file is a YAML document with a `db` key holding `host` and `port` subkeys. Parse it with the YAML module and print "<host>:<port>".

Input Format:
A multi-line YAML document with the structure: db: { host: <string>, port: <integer> }.

Output Format:
A single line: host, colon, port number.

Constraints:
host is a lowercase string 1..20 chars; 1 <= port <= 65535.
questions.sourcecode:
require "yaml"
data = $stdin.read
obj = YAML.load(data)
puts "#{obj['db']['host']}:#{obj['db']['port']}"

questions.title: Time Custom Strftime Format
questions.description:
Read six integers y mo d h mi s. Construct a Time object for that exact moment using Time.new, then print it formatted as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" using strftime.

Input Format:
Line 1: y mo d h mi s.

Output Format:
A 19-character timestamp string.

Constraints:
Valid Time arguments; year 1970..2100.
questions.sourcecode:
require "time"
y, mo, d, h, mi, s = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
t = Time.new(y, mo, d, h, mi, s)
puts t.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

questions.title: Benchmark Loop Versus Formula
questions.description:
Compute the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n two ways: (a) using a manual loop timed by Benchmark.measure; (b) using the closed-form formula n*(n+1)/2 timed by another Benchmark.measure. Compare both results and print "match" if they are equal, otherwise "mismatch".

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.

Output Format:
The single word "match" or "mismatch".

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 100000.
questions.sourcecode:
require "benchmark"
n = gets.to_i
loop_total = 0
Benchmark.measure { (1..n).each { |x| loop_total += x } }
formula_total = n * (n + 1) / 2
Benchmark.measure { formula_total = n * (n + 1) / 2 }
puts loop_total == formula_total ? "match" : "mismatch"

questions.title: JSON Multi-Document Aggregator
questions.description:
Read a target year on line 1, then a JSON array on line 2 of records each {"category":...,"amount":...,"date":"YYYY-MM-DD"}. Parse the JSON with the JSON module, parse each date with Date.new (split on '-'), filter records whose year matches the target, group amounts by category (summing), and print "<category> <total>" lines sorted by category.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer year. Line 2: a JSON array of records.

Output Format:
One line per category (matching the year), sorted by category name.

Constraints:
1 <= array length <= 100; 1 <= amount <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
require "json"
require "date"
year = gets.to_i
raw = gets.chomp
arr = JSON.parse(raw)
groups = {}
arr.each do |item|
  parts = item["date"].split("-").map(&:to_i)
  d = Date.new(parts[0], parts[1], parts[2])
  next unless d.year == year
  cat = item["category"]
  groups[cat] = 0 unless groups.key?(cat)
  groups[cat] += item["amount"]
end
keys = groups.keys.sort
keys.each { |k| puts "#{k} #{groups[k]}" }

questions.title: CSV Unique Column Values
questions.description:
Read n CSV rows each with a single column (a name). Write them to /tmp/atom_ruby_csv4.csv, read back with CSV.read, collect distinct values preserving first occurrence, then print all distinct values sorted ascending, one per line.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: a single name per line.

Output Format:
Distinct names sorted ascending, one per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; names are lowercase 1..20 chars.
questions.input3:
6
apple
banana
apple
cherry
banana
apple
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
lines = []
n.times { lines << gets.chomp }
path = "/tmp/atom_ruby_csv4.csv"
File.open(path, "w") do |f|
  lines.each { |l| f.puts(l) }
end
rows = File.readlines(path).map { |l| l.chomp.split(",") }
seen = {}
result = []
rows.each do |row|
  v = row[0]
  next if seen.key?(v)
  seen[v] = true
  result << v
end
result.sort.each { |v| puts v }

questions.title: Date Calendar Quarter Summary
questions.description:
Read n dates (each as y m d). For each, determine its calendar quarter (Q1 = Jan-Mar, Q2 = Apr-Jun, Q3 = Jul-Sep, Q4 = Oct-Dec). Count how many dates fall into each year-quarter bucket and print "<year>-Q<q> <count>" lines sorted ascending by the bucket key.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: y m d.

Output Format:
One line per distinct year-quarter bucket, sorted.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; valid dates 1970..2100.
questions.sourcecode:
require "date"
n = gets.to_i
counts = {}
n.times do
  y, m, d = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
  date = Date.new(y, m, d)
  q = (m - 1) / 3 + 1
  key = "#{date.year}-Q#{q}"
  counts[key] = 0 unless counts.key?(key)
  counts[key] += 1
end
keys = counts.keys.sort
keys.each { |k| puts "#{k} #{counts[k]}" }

questions.title: YAML Service List Sorter
questions.description:
A service registry is a YAML document with a `services` list; each entry has `name` and `port` keys. Parse it with the YAML module, sort entries by name ascending, and print "<name>=<port>" lines.

Input Format:
A multi-line YAML document with the structure: services: [ { name: <string>, port: <int> }, ... ].

Output Format:
One line per service, sorted by name: "name=port".

Constraints:
1 <= services.length <= 50; unique names.
questions.sampleinput1:
---
services:
  - name: alpha
    port: 8080
  - name: beta
    port: 3000
questions.input1:
---
services:
  - name: gamma
    port: 5000
  - name: delta
    port: 4000
questions.input2:
---
services:
  - name: b
    port: 1
  - name: a
    port: 2
  - name: c
    port: 3
questions.sourcecode:
require "yaml"
data = $stdin.read
obj = YAML.load(data)
services = obj["services"]
pairs = []
services.each { |s| pairs << [s["name"], s["port"]] }
pairs.sort.each { |name, port| puts "#{name}=#{port}" }
